title: Trees grown from seeds that orbited the Moon are just standing in US parks
hook: NASA lists a Pennsylvania park sycamore grown from a seed that orbited the Moon

open.title: NASA's Moon trees, forgotten for decades
open.line: In a Pennsylvania park, there's a sycamore tree.

summary: Apollo 14 carried tree seeds around the Moon in 1971. Planted across the US, many were largely forgotten until a teacher emailed NASA in 1996.

text: In a Pennsylvania park, there's a sycamore tree.
NASA's list says it grew from a Moon-orbiting seed.
In 1971, Apollo 14's Stuart Roosa took a can of seeds in his kit.
He'd been a Forest Service smokejumper.
He never landed. He orbited in the command module.
Five kinds, including pine, sycamore, redwood.
Back on Earth, the seed bags burst in decontamination.
The seeds were exposed to vacuum in the chamber.
Around 1976, they were planted across the US for the Bicentennial.
Some went to the White House, Brazil, Switzerland and Japan's Emperor.
But for decades, where many went was largely forgotten.
In 1996, a third-grade teacher and her class found a Moon Tree sign.
NASA's Dave Williams, who answered, had never heard of Moon trees.

sources: The Atlantic: We Almost Forgot About the Moon Trees
